blocks.text: # Proofpress harness adapters

One engine, three capture layers. The skill is the *rich* layer; the hook is the
*deterministic* layer; `ingest` is the catch-all. Install whichever your harness
supports — worst case you lose the *why*, never the *what*.

| Layer | Guarantee | What it captures |
|---|---|---|
| Skill (this directory) | model-discretionary, in-session | snapshot + structured claims + decision context (`--why` / `--rejected`) — testimony only the authoring agent can give |
| Hook (per-harness config) | deterministic, in-session | a snapshot always lands, even when the model forgets the skill |
| `proofpress ingest` | deterministic, out-of-session | teammates with nothing installed: every git commit becomes a ledger version |
## The agent contract (shared across all harnesses)

When you (the agent) create or substantially revise a **markdown knowledge
artifact** — ADRs, design docs, PRDs, strategy notes; **never code files** —
close the loop before yielding:

1. If the artifact has git history but no ledger entries: `python3 proofpress.py ingest <file>`.
2. Edit the file. Keep each block's `[//]: # (ob:xxxxxxxx)` anchor line attached

to blocks you keep or modify; drop anchors of blocks you delete; write no
   anchors for new blocks.
3. `python3 proofpress.py anchor <file>` — read the inherited / new / gone id
inventory it prints.
4. Write a claims JSON array — one entry per block you touched, honest over
flattering: `{"block": "<id>", "kind": "added|removed|modified|moved|unchanged", "note": "<one line>"}`.
5. Snapshot with testimony. `--why` and at least one `--rejected` (when you

considered alternatives) are **required, not optional** — this is the only
   moment the reasoning is cheap to capture:

```
   python3 proofpress.py snapshot <file> --kind agent --author <your-name> \
     --session <session-id> --note "<changelog line>" \
     --claims <claims.json> --why "<why this change>" \
     --rejected "<option — reason it was dropped>"
   ```
6. `python3 proofpress.py verify <file>` — report the output to the user

verbatim. **Never rewrite claims to force a green result**; a ⚠ is
   information for the reviewer, not a failure for you to hide.
Red line: never snapshot source-code files. That is git's territory.
## Install
- **Claude Code** — copy `claude-code/proofpress/` into `.claude/skills/`, and
merge `claude-code/hooks-example.json` into `.claude/settings.json`.
- **Codex CLI** — append `codex/AGENTS-snippet.md` to your `AGENTS.md`, and

merge `codex/config-hooks.toml` into `~/.codex/config.toml` (hooks GA since
  Codex v0.124).
- **Pi** — drop `pi/proofpress-skill.md` into your skills directory;

`pi/extension-skeleton.ts` sketches the deterministic in-process hook
  (untested skeleton — Pi's TS extension API moves fast, check current docs).

All adapters assume `proofpress.py` is reachable — vendored at the repo root or
installed on PATH as `git-proofpress` (any executable named `git-proofpress`
becomes `git proofpress`).
